strategies.name: Baseline Three-Stage All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Three sequential all-reduce operations (xm.REDUCE_SUM) with local per-shard scaling between each stage, totaling 3 dispatches. Straightforward approach with no fusion, moderate latency proportional to 3×log(W) communication rounds, largest total payload moved (3× full vector).

strategies.name: Fused Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Chain
strategies.desc: Replace first all-reduce with reduce-scatter to distribute W shards, apply local scaling to owned shard only, all-gather to broadcast, then repeat for remaining two stages. Uses 6 dispatches (3×RS + 3×AG) but significantly reduces bandwidth—each RS/AG moves 1/W of payload compared to full all-reduce, trading dispatch count for bandwidth efficiency.

strategies.name: Single All-Reduce with Buffered Scaling
strategies.desc: Allocate intermediate buffers for all three scaled states, perform one all-reduce on concatenated [original, intermediate1, intermediate2] tensor of shape (3×world_size×1024). Apply all scaling operations locally after single collective, reducing to 1 dispatch but tripling single-payload size and requiring 3× memory overhead.

strategies.name: Pipelined Two-Phase All-Reduce with Interleaved Ops
strategies.desc: Overlap second all-reduce with local scaling of first result by splitting tensor into chunks and dispatching AR(chunk[i]) while computing scale(chunk[i-1]). Uses 5-7 dispatches (chunked collectives) but hides O(W×S) compute latency within communication rounds, beneficial when computation is non-negligible relative to network time.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Intra-Node + Inter-Node Collectives
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node topology (num_nodes parameter): perform intra-node all-reduce within each node's cores_per_device×devices ranks first, then inter-node all-reduce across node representatives, then intra-node broadcast. Requires 9 dispatches (3 stages × 3 collectives each) but leverages faster intra-node interconnect bandwidth, reducing cross-node traffic by factor of cores_per_node.

def r1_fold_s1024_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 1024
    W = world_size
    dtype = x.dtype
    
    # Define per-shard scaling factors as a tensor for vectorized operations
    a = torch.tensor([1.0 + 0.5 * (r % 3) for r in range(W)], 
                     dtype=dtype, device=x.device)
    a_expanded = a.repeat_interleave(S)
    
    # Stage 1: First all-reduce
    s1 = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Apply a[r] / W scaling (vectorized)
    buf0 = s1 * a_expanded / W
    
    # Stage 2: Second all-reduce
    s2 = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf0)
    
    # Apply 1/W scaling (vectorized)
    buf1 = s2 / W
    
    # Stage 3: Third all-reduce
    out = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf1)
    
    return out
